correctness.rationale: The complete primary theorem and proof were reconstructed from the publisher PDF and its theorem page was visually inspected. Every stated hypothesis holds in the two-dimensional example: the original system is Parseval, K has closed range, R(U)=R(K), the controls commute, the image fusion space is closed, and the lower condition holds with delta one. Direct multiplication gives zero transformed analysis on every vector, so the conclusion fails. The disputed pseudo-inverse equality is exactly the projection identity onto R(K), exposing the missing adjoint-range condition.

value.rationale: Theorem 2.3 is an if-and-only-if construction criterion intended to recognize when operator transport preserves a controlled K-g-fusion frame. The counterexample satisfies the stated scalar lower condition with equality and R(U)=R(K), yet the transformed analysis vanishes identically. This isolates a structural distinction between the range of U and the range of its adjoint and yields a direct, mathematically motivated repair.
